note: Wikimedia Commons, “Saint Theonas I, metropolitan of Thessaloniki. icon in St Anastasia's monastery, 1836.jpg”; artist as recorded there: Unknown authorUnknown author — fetched 04 October 2026 at 1200px. The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: Commons names it an icon of «Saint Theonas I, metropolitan of Thessaloniki», painted 1836 in the monastery of St Anastasia the Deliverer from Potions — the house Theonas himself refounded, which is why his icon is there. This folder is that man: doxologia.ro prints «Sfântul Ierarh Teona, Arhiepiscopul Tesalonicului» for 4 April and saint.gr «Όσιος Θεωνάς Αρχιεπίσκοπος Θεσσαλονίκης» for the same day, reposed 4 April 1542. The ordinal I in Commons' title is what separates him from the later Theonas of the same see. The companion icons in that monastery were passed over because each puts him beside Anastasia or beside Gregory Palamas; this one is him alone. Commons describes it: Saint_Theonas_I,_metropolitan_of_Thessaloniki._icon_in_St_Anastasia's_monastery,_1836..
